name: Fourth Hall of Causality
reason: The source location 'Karma Hall' was localized as the 'Hall of Causality' (karma = causality); the episodes number its stages First through Fifth, and this entity is the fourth stage.
description: The fourth of the five deadly trial halls of the Hall of Causality in the Illusion Battlefield arc. Zane's group barely survives crossing it in Ep 1293, making it to the far bank after a brutal passage.

name: Godly Sigil
reason: The source's '[X] Seal Divine Dao' terms (e.g. 'Snow Seal Divine Dao', ch 1280) were split in localization into a 'Godly Sigil' (the seal a cultivator must be compatible with) plus a 'Godly Way of [X]' (the Dao itself).
description: A divine seal that tests a cultivator's compatibility before granting a Godly Way: in Ep 1299 a cultivator comprehends the Godly Sigil and obtains the Godly Way of Snow, while in Ep 1300 Zane is told he is 'not compatible with the Godly Sigil' (mirroring the source's 'You are not compatible with the Snow Seal Divine Dao'). An 'Unrivaled Godly Sigil' is also earned in Ep 1301.

name: Saint Spear
reason: The source term 'Holy Spear' (as in the Holy Spear of Massacre, chs 1149-1297) was localized as 'Saint Spear' for the Western fantasy register.
description: A sacred spear lineage appearing in Ep 1308 as the name of an organization, the Order of the Saint Spear, whose first glimmer of hope in a long time is tied to Hailey's chance at freedom.

name: Five Elements Power
reason: The source term 'Five Elements Power' (ch 976) was retained verbatim in the adaptation.
description: The combined power of the five elements, prized because it has no absolute weakness; entire holy grounds in the upper world build their defensive arrays from it (Ep 999), and in Ep 1000 a light appears that can suppress all Five Elements Power in the world.

name: Echo Beasts
reason: The source divine beast 'Howling Celestial Tapir' (ch 995), whose rarity governs the supply of Roaring Tokens, was renamed 'Echo Beast' to fit the Western fantasy register while keeping the sound motif.
description: Rare divine creatures whose roars carry the Law of Causality across the entire universe, producing Roaring Tokens as a natural byproduct (Ep 1018). When they were plentiful, tokens were cheap enough to abuse; Magnus, who farms tokens from his own stash of Echo Beasts, has only a little over a hundred on hand.

name: Illusory Array
reason: A generic cultivation-world formation concept carried over from the source's illusion arrays for the Western fantasy setting.
description: A class of array formation that generates illusions around a physical body; in Ep 1033 Fenton contrasts an ordinary Illusory Array with a mirror-like phenomenon that works on a different principle.

name: Regis-Bane
reason: The adaptation coined the proper name 'Regis-Bane' (evoking a king-slaying blade) for a sword the source describes only descriptively as the sword of the Sovereign King of the Empire (ch ~1016).
description: Fenton's crimson jade sword, a Low Grade-One Divine-Class weapon forged long ago from the very lifeblood of an Emperor of a tenth-grade divine kingdom (Eps 1034-1037). Its formidable aura is built on a monarch's comprehension forged into steel, which proves no match for Zane's genuine Chaos World soul pressure.

name: Purification Pool
reason: The source's 'Clear Growth Pool' (also rendered 'Clear Sage Pool' in chs 1051-1052) was renamed 'Purification Pool' to plainly convey its soul-cleansing function in the Western fantasy register.
description: A pool at the Thirteen Palaces that cultivators must enter before the Passing the Torch inheritance; it clears the soul and doubles comprehension for a short time. In Ep 1074 the impatient overseer threatens to seal the Purification Pool if the latecomer (Zane) does not show up soon.

name: Tribulation Exterminating Pill
reason: The source pill 'Calamity Annihilation Pill' (chs 1053-1082) was localized as 'Tribulation Exterminating Pill', a near-literal rendering in the adaptation's register.
description: A rare pill from the Thirteen Palaces arc (Eps 1076-1079), corresponding to the source's Calamity Annihilation Pill tied to the Torch Flame inheritance storyline.

name: Greater Celestial Tribulations
reason: The source's major 'Heavenly Tribulation' (as opposed to the 'minor Heavenly Tribulation', chs 908-978) was localized as the 'Greater Celestial Tribulations'.
description: The full-scale heavenly tribulations a cultivator must survive at major breakthroughs, far deadlier than minor tribulations. In Ep 942 Zane learns Amber is facing hers, and even with her incredible talent the Greater Celestial Tribulations are no joke.

name: Unburdened Blade
reason: The adaptation gave the proper name 'The Unburdened Blade' to the source's unnamed basic swordsmanship that Luo Zheng keeps stripping down to its essence.
description: An advanced set of basic swordsmanship Zane is refining (Ep 465): after a breakthrough in the upper world, he believes it can be simplified even further, stripped down to its absolute essence.

name: Black Tortoises
issues: Shares its name with the legendary Four Cardinal Beasts' Black Tortoise (Ep 282); these are mundane, slow trial beasts (source chs ~450-456), so the two should not be merged in the sheet.
reason: The source beast name 'Black Tortoise' was carried over directly; these mentions are the plural for the beast species.
description: Slow, heavily armored beasts encountered in the trial arc around Eps 465-468; in Ep 468 another creature's only weakness is being even slower than the Black Tortoises.

name: Discipline of Vile Malice
reason: The adaptation named Stoney's dark martial path the 'Discipline of Vile Malice', an evocative rendering of the source's sinister ghost-arts cultivation in this arc (chs ~454-458).
description: Stoney's dark cultivation path, a soul-based attack system that includes the Skull Ghost Hand (Eps 469-470). In Ep 469 an old man doubts Zane's soul has developed enough to resist it.

name: Elder Luna
reason: The source's 'Mysterious Yin Old Man', the 900-plus-year-old legend heading the Mysterious Yin Mansion (ch 468), was localized as 'Elder Luna', with 'Luna' rendering the yin/moon element of his sect's name (localized as the Mysterious Luna Hall).
description: Head of the Mysterious Luna Hall, a fourth-grade sect, and a living legend who has walked the earth for over nine hundred years (nearly 976) while keeping jet-black hair. He leads an expedition in Eps 481-484 and has accumulated secrets most cultivators cannot fathom; in Ep 550 he vanishes completely.

name: Festival of Illumination
reason: The source's 'Lantern Lighting Festival' (also rendered 'Lantern Festival', chs 388-516) was renamed the 'Festival of Illumination' to fit the Western fantasy register.
description: A recurring festival (Eps 483, 531) corresponding to the source's Lantern Festival, during which the spirit lamps of an ancient tomb light up; the number of lamps that ignite each festival has grown over the centuries.

name: Philip
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Philip', a steady, scholarly name fitting the sect's analytical eldest disciple.
description: The eldest disciple of the Ethereal Spirit Sect (Eps 485-493), an analytical observer who assesses Zane's threat level alongside Brent, calmly disputing his sect-mates' dismissals of the newcomer's strength.

name: Relic-grade
issues: Name drift: Ep 493 says 'Relic-grade' for the tier-6 weapon class, while later delivered episodes (e.g. Ep 1034) use the canonical 'Relic-Class'.

name: Blazing Thunder Prison
reason: The adaptation's name for a lethal lightning punishment in the tomb-trial arc; no proper source name surfaced in the evidence.
description: A brutal death sentence dispensed by the trial discs in Eps 538-539, so powerful that even a Life-and-Death Realm master would not bet on surviving it.

name: Spirit-Tribulation-level
reason: The source cultivation stage 'Void Tribulation Realm' was localized as 'Spirit Tribulation'; Ep 748's army-formation line directly adapts ch 725, mapping Divine Reflection/Divine Core/Void Tribulation to War General-level/Inner-Core/Spirit-Tribulation.
description: The adjectival form of the Spirit Tribulation cultivation stage (Eps 546-941); in Ep 748 Spirit-Tribulation warriors fly highest above the advancing square formations, outranking War General-level and Inner-Core fighters.

name: Borgan
reason: The source demon warrior 'Yinna' (ch 555), the arena challenger whose gaze lands on Luo Zheng, was localized to the harsh, brutish name 'Borgan' fitting a demon-kin arena bully.
description: A demon-kin arena challenger in the Tower of Sin arc (Eps 569-570) who turns his challenge on Zane and is killed with a single, effortless sidestep and counter; the watching creatures are unsurprised by his death.

name: Absolute Madness
reason: The adaptation's name for the Orcs' berserk battle state from the source's Sea God Continent arena arc; no proper source term surfaced in the evidence.
description: A berserk state the Orcs can enter (Ep 622): once an Orc goes into Absolute Madness, it will not stop until its target is dead, or it is.

name: Moon Shadow Begonia
reason: The source treasure name 'Moon Shadow Begonia' was retained verbatim in the adaptation.
description: A treasured flower sought in Eps 645-646, which for Zane turns out to have been merely an opportunity of convenience; in the source its effects are speculated to underlie Liu Yu's rise to the top of the Spirit Sea Realm.

name: Crabstone Amulet
reason: The adaptation's name for a protective amulet from the source's Mysterious Underworld Cave arc; no proper source name surfaced in the evidence.
description: A strange gem amulet Yolande slips over Zane's head (Ep 662), the only thing keeping the group alive against the Death Light outside their refuge; panic erupts in Ep 671 when it ends up locked inside a lost Storage Ring.

name: Flaming and Dread Places
issues: Not a single entity: the surface is a coordination of two Ogre strongholds, the Flaming Place and the Dread Place ('the Flaming and Dread Places of the Ogres', Ep 666; 'every last Ogre from both the Flaming and Dread Places', Ep 948), parallel to the Violet Heart Sanctuary of the humans and the Sanctum of Eternal Night of the Twilight Group.
reason: Dropped as a conjoined phrase; the underlying individual stronghold names, not this compound, would be the canonical entities.

name: Lumen
reason: One of the three great human-race leaders of the upper world (source: the Empyreans Oracle, Original Sin and Thunder Law, ch 652) was localized to the light-themed name 'Lumen'; Yolande's service to Lumen best matches Yun Luo's service under Empyrean Original Sin, master of the Tower of Sin.
description: Leader of the second-largest of the three great forces of the divided human race in the upper world, commanding three thousand realms against Malachi's four thousand and Soren's two thousand (Ep 671). Yolande serves Lumen, and the real brewing conflict is between Malachi and Lumen; in Ep 674 factions maneuver to place Zane at Lumen's side.

name: Duskshell Clam
reason: The source water beast 'Black and Blue Mussel' (also rendered Black-Green/Black-Cyan Mussel, chs 663-665) was renamed 'Duskshell Clam', a cleaner Western fantasy creature name keeping the dark-shell image.
description: A level-four water demonic beast hunted in the Fish Dragon Sect's sea trial (Eps 683-684): a weak fighter protected by a legendarily tough shell, which may yield a Shadow Pearl, a priceless pill-crafting ingredient.

name: Wray
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to the short, rugged US-origin name 'Wray' for a minor warrior in the sea-trial arc.
description: A warrior in the Fish Dragon Sect sea-trial ambush (Eps 685-686); Bernard shouts a warning to him when Tessa suddenly switches targets and attacks.

name: Silvermoon Pavilion
reason: The adaptation's name for an eatery in the city arc around Ep 689; no proper source name surfaced in the evidence.
description: A dining establishment used as a measure of wealth in Ep 689: with one crystal, a man could have bought the entire Silvermoon Pavilion and eaten like a king every day for years.

name: House Ward
reason: The source aristocratic 'Wu Family' (ch 703), one of the four families Ning Yudie cows into tribute, was localized as 'House Ward' in line with the show's Legacy House naming.
description: One of the aristocratic Legacy Houses squeezed by Tia for an enormous tribute of Aether crystals (Eps 722-723); its ashen-faced lord protests that House Ward could never gather that many.

name: War General-level
reason: In Ep 748's army-formation line, which directly adapts ch 725, 'War General-level' replaces the source's 'Divine Reflection' warriors (with Inner-Core for Divine Core and Spirit-Tribulation for Void Tribulation).
description: A power tier used for rank-and-file fighters (Eps 734-748): in the great square formations of independent warriors, War General-level fighters advance lowest, below Inner-Core masters and Spirit-Tribulation warriors.

name: Abel
reason: The source's Xingjian (Star-Sword) Esteemed Cultivator, whom the Heartless Monk brings along to interrogate Luo Zheng (chs 751-752), was localized to the US-origin name 'Abel'.
description: An old friend of Lord Wallace who comes along for the ride when invited (Eps 773-775). He possesses a soul-searching technique that can tear a mind wide open, which Wallace wants used on Zane; Wallace's talk of Zane stirs his curiosity.

name: Crane City
reason: The source's 'Lonely Crane City' (also rendered 'Solitary Crane City', chs 758-782) was shortened to 'Crane City' for the adaptation.
description: A great city in the Divine Kingdom arc (Eps 797-805), corresponding to the source's Lonely Crane City, second-largest city of the Black Iron Divine Kingdom and home of the Profound Jade Martial House; in Ep 805 a desperate man rushes there seeking someone of real power.

name: Sevenwaters Forest
reason: The source location 'Seven Waters Forest' (ch 803) was retained with the compound spelling 'Sevenwaters Forest'.
description: The forest where a monstrous-looking child was abandoned right after birth because of his appearance (Eps 823-826), matching the source's Seven Waters Forest backstory.
